title: Coefficient-stability-based multiclass spectral selection for complementary terahertz discrimination of medicinal materials
title_zh: 面向中药材太赫兹辅助判别的系数稳定性多类别光谱选择
abstract: Established medicinal-material identification relies on morphological, microscopic and chemical tests. We developed a coefficient-stability-based multiclass selection strategy for complementary terahertz discrimination. Absorption and refractive-index exports covered 1,672 measured medicinal-material specimens in 18 workbooks. For 300 balanced five-source Suanzaoren TRAIN specimens, classwise coefficient consistency over 20 Monte Carlo draws ranked spectral coordinates; feature budgets and SVM parameters were selected within repeated nested validation. Three fivefold partitions with two inner folds produced 900 related predictions. Selected absorption achieved 93.44% mean accuracy with 220.6 of 612 coordinates on average. The same-partition full-spectrum SVM achieved 82.67%, establishing a 10.78-percentage-point gain against this matched reference. Full-spectrum shrinkage LDA achieved 91.78% (MC20-minus-LDA interval: −1.11 to 4.44 percentage points). Across outer refits, selected absorption had descriptive Nogueira stability Φ = 0.8360. Complementary full-spectrum protocols examined grouping and supervision: workbook-held-out accuracy was 98.84% for Suanzaoren–Zaoren and 65.61% across four materials; ten valid labels per class increased query accuracy from 80.00% to 83.78% with source scaling and kernel scale frozen. These representation, candidate-pool, grouping and label-update effects connect discrimination to identifiable analysis choices. The reusable ranking interface and SVM evidence provide a methodological reference for developing further medicinal-material classifiers and validation on independent acquisitions.
science_scope: Current corrected collection; E1 same-ID bridge; distinct LOWO and support protocols; no scientific training performed during revision
